A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAFCOR study. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated figures.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original MNIST and Fashion-MNIST experiments comparing privacy regimes and robust aggregation methods under malicious-worker attacks.

after.justification: The original learning experiments remain, with additional SMEA comparisons and an original aggregation-runtime study in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes its loop condition from sum(c_i) > n−2f to sum(c_i) ≥ n−2f, allowing another filtering iteration at equality. CAFCOR's noise mechanism, momentum updates, and remaining aggregation procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST and Fashion-MNIST with the same classification tasks, privacy regimes, attack families, and heterogeneity scenarios. The added runtime measurements vary model dimension without introducing another dataset or task domain.

E2.justification: SMEA, previously discussed theoretically, joins the MNIST aggregation comparisons in Figures 7–9. Existing comparators remain. New Table 1 compares CAF, SMEA, Meamed, and GM using averaging as the runtime reference.

E3.justification: The new runtime comparison uses 30 workers, including 3 malicious workers, and dimensions of 2.5, 5, and 10 million, measuring time relative to averaging. The existing accuracy experiments retain their stated models, preprocessing, training budgets, and privacy settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 extends the aggregation-replacement analysis to SMEA and adds a three-dimension runtime analysis examining computational scaling. The existing attack and heterogeneity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds, numbered 1–5, and standard-deviation reporting. Added SMEA curves use the existing uncertainty-band format. The runtime table introduces no additional replication information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 7–9 add SMEA results and substantially revise CAFCOR curves under unchanged stated settings: Figure 7b ends near 92% in v1 versus 84% in v2, while Figure 9b changes from about 79% to 87%. Table 1 adds runtime results; at dimension 10 million, CAF and SMEA take respectively 100 and 117,255 times the averaging runtime.

T1.justification: Appendix B changes the termination argument from weight sum ≤ n−2f after 2f iterations to < n−2f after 2f+1 iterations, matching the revised loop condition. The propositions, assumptions, and privacy/utility bounds remain unchanged. Earlier 'at most 2f' wording persists in the proof and Section 4.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: CAFCOR combines privacy and robustness using shared randomness, approaches central-DP utility, and improves upon local-DP utility. The added empirical evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New discussion argues that one-time quadratic seed exchange has negligible cost and interprets CAF's advantage over similarly accurate SMEA as computational efficiency. Section 4.1 adds a collusion-granularity explanation, but describes q workers as non-curious although Theorem 4.1 uses q for colluding workers.

D1.justification: Section 1.2 newly specifies that the one-time seed exchange transmits integers and has quadratic communication cost, adding limited setup information. The power-method implementation, training details, and intention to release code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Allouah et al.'s work on tight error bounds and breakdown points under data heterogeneity. It revises comparisons with Sabater et al. and Allouah et al. concerning communication topology and collusion granularity. The existing trilemma paper's change from 2023b to 2023c is citation relabeling.

P1.justification: Localized edits adjust abstract terminology, expand related-work and privacy-analysis discussion, and add the SMEA discussion. Correspondence information and the conference edition are corrected. The main section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 7–9 are redrawn with SMEA curves and expanded legends, and Table 1 is added. Figures 10–12 are relocated without changing their results. Algorithm 2's input formatting is tightened, and references gain colored-link styling.

improvement.justification: The SMEA comparison and runtime table strengthen evidence for CAF's computational advantage, and the stopping-condition edit addresses a proof boundary case. However, v2 leaves Figure 2a near 79% while revised Figure 9b reaches about 87% for the same stated MNIST setting. This unexplained inconsistency, together with conflicting 2f versus 2f+1 termination wording, makes the net quality effect uncertain.
